title: Baby Shark
reason: 20th-century camp song with no documented pre-1931 publication; the famous recording, arrangement and video belong to Pinkfong. Korean courts found the underlying folk chant was not owned by SmartStudy, but that does not meet our pre-1931 rule. License the Pinkfong version or skip.
owner_if_known: The Pinkfong Company (formerly SmartStudy) for the popular version

title: The Wheels on the Bus
reason: Written by Verna Hills (1898-1990); earliest known publication December 1937 (American Childhood). Published after 1930 and the author died after 1955.

title: If You're Happy and You Know It
reason: No publication found before 1957; copyright registration filed in 1971 crediting Joe Raposo (Jonico Music). Fails the pre-1931 rule.

title: Itsy Bitsy Spider
reason: Text first printed in 1910 as the 'Spider Song' with different wording; the familiar words and tune are documented only from 1948 (Western Folklore; American Folk Songs for Children). The pre-1931 publication of the tune is not documented. Probably traditional, but get legal sign-off before use.
owner_if_known: None known (traditional); 1948 songbook arrangements may be protected

title: Head, Shoulders, Knees and Toes
reason: Words cited as an exercise in 1912 (The Children's Friend), but the sung version and its tune pairing are not documented before 1931. Uncertain.

title: Five Little Ducks
reason: Origin and author unknown; no publication found before Raffi's 1982 release. Uncertain.
owner_if_known: None known; Raffi's 1982 arrangement is protected

title: Five Little Monkeys Jumping on the Bed
reason: Folk chant with no documented pre-1931 publication; popular versions follow Eileen Christelow's books (1989 onward). Uncertain.
owner_if_known: None known for the chant; Christelow's books are protected

title: Five Little Speckled Frogs
reason: Origin unknown; the earliest documented reference is 1978. Fails the pre-1931 rule.

title: I'm a Little Teapot
reason: Written by George Harry Sanders and Clarence Z. Kelley; published 1939. Fails the pre-1931 rule.

title: The Ants Go Marching
reason: The tune ('When Johnny Comes Marching Home', 1863) is public domain, but the children's lyrics have no documented pre-1931 publication. Uncertain.

title: Down by the Station
reason: Credited to Paul Mills and Slim Gaillard (recorded 1947, written 1948); only reportedly seen in a 1931 issue of Recreation. Not published before 1931.
owner_if_known: Paul Mills / Slim Gaillard (publisher not confirmed)

title: Do Your Ears Hang Low?
reason: Tune ('Turkey in the Straw' / 'Zip Coon', 1834-38) is public domain, but the children's 'ears' lyrics are undated (a bawdy variant dates from about 1900). Uncertain.

title: We Wish You a Merry Christmas
reason: The famous tune is missing from every carol anthology before 1935; the modern version comes from Arthur Warrell's arrangement, published by OUP in 1935. Warrell died in 1939, so it is likely public domain in the EU, but a 1935 US publication is protected until 2031.

title: When the Saints Go Marching In
reason: Traditional spiritual first recorded in 1923 (Paramount Jubilee Singers); no confirmed pre-1931 printing of this version, and later copyright claims (Presley, Stamps, Winsett) are unresolved. Uncertain.
owner_if_known: Claims by Luther G. Presley / Virgil O. Stamps / R. E. Winsett (status unclear)

title: Hush, Little Baby
reason: Traditional Southern US lullaby; earliest documentation is Cecil Sharp's notation from 1918, and a pre-1931 publication of the familiar version is not confirmed. Probably traditional, but get sign-off.
